stages.title: Phase 1: audit and mini-WDA
stages.note: Baseline R 72.2 / S 7.7, root causes RC1–RC15, fixes in five PRs. mini-WDA is WDA 16.14.1 code compiled for macOS.

stages.title: Phase 2 and 2b: on-device verification
stages.note: Simulator and iPhone 13 Pro Max agreed on all 246 cases. Found RC-D1 (documented as DRIFT) and RC-D2 (skipped).

children.title: Simulator run, RC-D2 fix and RC-D1 note
Real iPhone: same outcomes as the simulator

stages.title: Phase 3: lookup time vs screen size
stages.note: Class chain 22–29 % faster at 100–2000 elements; 70 to 676 ms per lookup on the iPhone.

stages.title: Phase 4: plain LLMs vs the converter
stages.note: No model beats the converter on R; models win S but emit 4–43 wrong chains.

stages.title: Phase 5: fixes from Phase 4
stages.note: R 95.8 / S 92.0 at the end of stage C; prompt v4 reaches 96–97 % of the converter with 0 wrong chains for Sonnet and Opus.

children.title: C1: device check of doubtful forms
C2: fixes for what C1 confirmed
D: measure again, prompt v2 to v4

stages.title: Phase 6: monthly upstream watch
stages.note: Estimate was about 1–1.5 h. A GitHub Action compares Appium, driver and WDA releases and opens an issue only when something important changed.

stages.title: Phase 7: GitHub corpus
stages.note: Planned about 2.5–3 h, about 30 % of one window. Released as 1.0.3.

children.title: Harvest: 78 reused literals and new iOS projects
Offline check of scanner and converter

stages.title: Publishing: npm, two articles, playground
stages.note: npm 1.0.0–1.0.2, short README, dev.to articles on the converter and on the LLM comparison, GitHub Pages playground (#60).

stages.title: Architecture review
stages.note: Reasons for every skip, CI harness, validator split, one XPath lexer in two steps, scanText. Changed nothing on the corpus.

stages.title: Code review 1
stages.note: Ten findings in lib/: eight fixed in nine PRs, one a no-op, one left to fix-on-touch. Changed nothing on the corpus.

stages.title: Code review 2
stages.note: A review of #70–#78: five of its eight findings were regressions of review 1. This is what produced the Scope of fixes rule and the stop criterion.

stages.title: Scope of fixes rule and known-issues backlog
Release 1.0.4
stages.note: Tag v1.0.4, GitHub release, npm latest is 1.0.4.

stages.title: Maintenance mode
stages.note: Triggers: (a) a new Appium, xcuitest-driver or WDA release (the monthly watch opens an issue), (b) a user report, (c) a release. A P1 is fixed; everything else waits in the backlog. No new phases, refactors or review rounds unprompted.
stages.prompt: Read ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the project memory (project-maintenance-mode.md, fix-scope-limit.md, estimate-calibration.md), docs/known-issues.md and docs/plan.json. Check that the last release PR is merged and the tag exists. The project is in maintenance mode: work only on a trigger (an `upstream` issue about a new Appium, xcuitest-driver or WDA release, a user report, or a release). Task: (describe the trigger here). Conditions: fix now only what gives a silently wrong result or a crash on realistic input and show it with such an input; everything else goes to docs/known-issues.md; one review round per change set; a new branch and a PR; give the estimate first and wait for yes.

stages.note: Parked until user feedback. P1 (Other Tools page) is merged; P2d (xcuitest-driver #3052) is open.
